BiblicalUsage: Nimrod is the first mighty one after the flood, a son of Cush who began to be mighty in the earth and a mighty hunter before the LORD. His name becomes a byword — even as Nimrod the mighty hunter — and the same record stands in the chronicle of the tribes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Nimrod is a warning wrapped in a compliment: mighty before the LORD, yet the father of Babel, and his might ends in a tower God scatters.
